answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust slow and expensive to grow: each identity locks a stake that is released only gradually, like a glacier thawing, and earns a higher transaction limit only through a steady pulse of independently verified useful work over weeks. A newcomer starts with tiny limits, so spawning thousands of copies multiplies the locked capital and the waiting time instead of influence. Like yarrow spreading across a field, reputation expands by persistence, not sudden multiplication, so a sybil flood becomes costly and slow.
